2025年12月24日。25年的平安夜，多肉全成就了。
起始于2025年1月份。第一批成就是1月29日解锁的，以此推算，大概是1月中旬开始做成就的吧。
反正就是差不多25年一整年，多肉全成就了。
内心的感觉还是蛮奇特：一方面全成就是只靠时间堆积就可以解锁了，说到底，并没有什么值得骄傲的；但另一方面，毕竟是花了一年的时间来完成的——虽然只是做到了每天早晚登录一下，看植物缺水了就浇浇水，然后就下线的程度——总归是对这一年的“打卡”有个交待吧。
像是背了一年的背包，目的地到了，也就可以脱下了，心里也算是如释重负了。
而且，平安夜做完全成就，还是蛮开心的。最近也试着在家里种一下虎皮兰、七里香和绿萝了，希望她们能好好成长吧，也希望接下来的每一年都能好好过吧。也祝愿所有的朋友们平安顺遂、椿萱并茂、棠棣同馨。

This is one of those games that are simply a gem in the rough, especially since it's free to play.

TLDR: Ultimate Zen mode, add it to your library right this second, you don't even know how badly you need this game.

[h1] The Graphics[/h1]

Honestly, simplicity is bliss and this game definitely has simplicity in mind when it comes to graphics. The pots have cute designs, but they're definitely not over complicated, the plants are unique and all have detail. Even the little snail that happily chugs his (or her) way around your pot looks adorable! This game has a cute factor that's actually mind blowing, it's the ultimate stress reliever, even in the graphics department.

[h1] Gameplay[/h1]

This is a game that's all about patience. You can't go into Viridi with a mentality such as an action or adventure game, this game requires patience because your plants will grow in real-time. Yes, real-time. You water your plants once a day (even your snail if you like, but he's pretty good on his own so I wouldn't bother the lil guy). You watch the background change in real-time, it follows your system clock so if it's night time outside, it'll be dark in the game, same with day time. Viridi has a simple mechanic for gameplay, you water your plants, you listen to the calming music, and you enter your happy place. 

[h1] Story[/h1]

Completely nonexistent. You make your own story out of your plants and your little snail friend, that's the bottom line.

[h1] Mod Support[/h1]

As far as I know, this is also nonexistent.

[h1] Summary[/h1]

So what are you getting with a game like this? Well, this is your happy place. you go to this game from time to time so you can relax from the natural stress in your daily life. The gameplay is simplistic, the visuals are beautiful and you will absolutely love this game if these things sound appealing to you. Also, there's achievements available, they take time to accomplish because of the real-time aspect of the game, but they're rewarding once you achieve them!

Do I recommend this game? Highly, especially if you're craving some stress relief. This is the ultimate test of patience, and there's a little gift every week for your patience as well. An extra seed to grow a new plant!

Viridi Is a very simplistic game, a relaxing game that keeps you occupied without giving you a rushed feel. Although there will be in-game purchases you do get a lot out of the free experience. 


[h1]Quick Summary[/h1]
You create a plant pot, each one has its own design and the ability to name it. Every pot comes with its own snail which you can sing to and water just like the plants (I don't really know why you'd water a snail unless snails can get dried up, which I guess they could? You wouldn't want a crusty snail.) Once a week you get one free seedling. These free seedlings are 100% random and give that little feeling of excitement every time you open one. 

[h1]In game purchases[/h1]
Like most free games, In-Game purchases are a large part in the overall game. Besides the once weekly seedling the only way to get new plants would be to purchase them with (I assume this goes this goes w/o saying) real money. This has not bothered me too much as you can still get the relaxing part of the game down, although it can get rather bothersome to know every individual plant would come out of your paycheck. If you reall get into the game, I'm sure you wouldn't regret purchasing some plants or new areas. 


[h1]The waiting game[/h1]
One thing that really keeps you on your toes is the wait for your seedlings to up and have ther little spurts of growth. The growth of your succulent brings out the ultimate reward in Viridi. Although patience is key, it does not come w/o its hardships and rewards, which I think Viridi expresses perfectly.

[h1]Would I recommend Viridi[/h1]
I'm personally very attached to succulents and have friends who do enjoy plants just as much as I, and because of that I would recommend this game. Viridi is a good game, one that I'd love to see others enjoy and although this game is not without its flaws I liked Viridi and I'm sure many others do aswell.

Sometimes I would check on my plants in Viridi once a day and water the thirsty ones. Sometimes I would skip 4 or 5 days. It didn't seem to make a difference in their health. I'm guessing if you waited like a week some of the plants would really die? Can't answer that because I did not give it that long. I like the music. I like the playback feature-- you can re-watch your plants grow from when you last had the game open. Graphics are okay: the plant's colors become vibrant when you water them and they show some signs of withering when dry, although the game's backgrounds are quite plain. You can purchase other backgrounds (with real money) to better accommodate your tastes. Viridi gives you some free plants but you can also buy more. It also gives you a few pots to pick from but if you want more you'll have to buy them with real cash. Overall, this is a pretty bare-bones game even if you did buy a few of the extras. It's meant to be a chill game, I get that. But it's so chill that it really has no point. In real life simply throw on some cool Spotify tunes, take an interesting plant from outside, bring it inside, put it in a pot, and enjoy the free oxygen and style it adds to your room... ta-da, real-life Viridi with real life bonus benefits.
